oneliner.t: Republican former U.S. senator (2003–2009) and three-term NH-1 congressman, a Boston Scientific director since 2009, who won the Sept. 8, 2026 GOP primary with Trump's endorsement and faces Democrat Chris Pappas for the seat he lost to Jeanne Shaheen in 2008.

born.t: September 10, 1964, Boston, Massachusetts (Wikipedia; AP gave his age as 61 in October 2025, consistent)

upbringing.t: Sununu is one of eight children of John H. Sununu, later New Hampshire governor and White House chief of staff, and Nancy Hayes Sununu; his brother Chris Sununu was a four-term governor. His father's side is of Lebanese, Greek and Hispanic ancestry, and Wikipedia describes him as the first Palestinian American to serve in Congress. He earned B.S. (1986) and M.S. (1987) degrees in mechanical engineering at MIT and a Harvard MBA (1991). Before Congress he worked in high-tech, including at a company of Dean Kamen's, and was chief financial officer of Teletrol Systems, a maker of building-control systems.

career.role: Engineer in high-tech industry, including a Dean Kamen company; chief financial officer of Teletrol Systems
U.S. Representative, NH-1 (Appropriations; Budget Committee vice chairman)
U.S. Senator (Finance; Commerce; Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs; Joint Economic); youngest senator; lost 2008 re-election
Member, Congressional Oversight Panel for TARP (appointed by Mitch McConnell)
Director (initial pay about $60,000 retainer plus about $120,000 in annual stock)

career.org: Akin Gump Strauss Hauer & Feld (law and lobbying firm)
Saint Anselm College; Waterville Valley Ski Resort

platform.t: Focus on the cost of housing, health care and energy; protect Social Security, Medicare and veterans' services.
'Lower the temperature' in Washington; term limits for Congress ('No more career politicians').
Opposes raising taxes to cut the deficit; defends the One Big Beautiful Bill Act as keeping taxes low.
Opposes the trade war with Canada; says tariffs should be set at a 'reasonable rate' with congressional involvement.
Says he would not have started the war with Iran but that preventing an Iranian nuclear weapon is a long-run U.S. interest.
Declined to take a position on aid to Israel, calling it complex.
Supports limiting birthright citizenship (by Congress if the courts don't) and proof of citizenship to vote (SAVE Act, voter ID).
More domestic production, pipelines, transmission lines and permitting reform.
Calls China the biggest national-security threat; supports more military aid to Taiwan; backed the capture of Maduro.
Supports excluding transgender women from girls' sports; says the federal government should leave marijuana to the states.

promises.t: Lower the cost of housing, health care and energy.
Protect Social Security, Medicare and veterans' services.
Be an independent senator ('I don't need an appointment or a job').

claims.claim: Has spent the last 16 years in the private sector — tech firms, small businesses, the Waterville Valley ski area and college teaching.

record.t: Left the Senate in 2009; has worked in tech, taught at Saint Anselm College and sat on boards including Boston Scientific and his family's Waterville Valley resort. The list leaves out his 2010 Akin Gump policy-adviser role and his corporate directorships (Boston Scientific, Time Warner Cable, Lloyd's of London council).

claims.claim: New Hampshire is 'dead last in highway funding in New England' after Pappas's eight years on the Transportation Committee.
claims.short: NH last in NE highway funding

record.t: Fox News reported that federal and state figures put New Hampshire among the lowest in total and per-capita road and bridge funding nationally, but not last on every measure.

claims.claim: Pappas votes almost exclusively with party leaders.

record.t: In the 119th Congress Pappas voted with his party on 89.7% of party-line votes and crossed party lines 48 times. The Lugar Center ranked him the most bipartisan House Democrat in 2023.

claims.claim: Pappas has 'attempted very little in Congress' and 'accomplished even less.'

record.t: A characterization. For context: Pappas sponsored 59 bills in the 119th Congress (through Sept. 30, 2026), 1 of which passed the House.

claims.claim: Has written and passed legislation under presidents and Congresses of both parties.

record.t: He sponsored the New England Wilderness Act (2006, Bush era). His role in Clinton-era laws (e.g. the Internet Tax Freedom Act) is documented only in his Boston Scientific company bio. congress.gov was not reachable.
No record either way was found.

claims.claim: The One Big Beautiful Bill did not add trillions to the debt.

said.where: Citizens Count issue summary (position on raising taxes to reduce the deficit)

record.t: CBO estimated the law will increase deficits by $2.8 trillion through 2034. It also raised the debt limit by $5 trillion.

claims.claim: First elected to the Senate at 38, its youngest member.

record.t: Elected in 2002 at 38; the youngest senator ('Baby of the Senate') 2003–2009.

said.t: Wrote a Union Leader op-ed titled 'Donald Trump is a loser' on the eve of the 2024 NH primary and backed Nikki Haley.

did.t: Accepted Trump's endorsement for the 2026 Senate primary; has largely avoided discussing it.
Says the 2005 Bush privatization plan would have kept the system solvent had it passed, but that it now needs bipartisan solutions.

entries.t: National co-chair of John Kasich's presidential campaign.
Endorsed Nikki Haley; op-ed 'Donald Trump is a loser'.
Said he'd want support 'across the entire spectrum', including the president: 'We'll cross that bridge when we get to it.'
Endorsed by Trump (Feb. 1); breaks with him on the Canada trade war and the Iran war; says he doesn't 'need anyone from outside New Hampshire' to campaign for him.
Joined Democrats in filibustering the Patriot Act renewal conference report.
Supported the Patriot Act 'with additional civil safeguards'.
Backed private-account reform (per his 2026 description of the 2005 plan).
Pledges to protect Social Security; calls for bipartisan fixes.
Voted against renewing the assault-weapons ban (2004) and against the Federal Marriage Amendment (2006).

aipac_endorse.t: Not found — AIPAC is not listed among his endorsers on Wikipedia's race page (as of 2026-10-14); AIPAC's own page was not checked.

aipac_pac.note: career — not checked (Track AIPAC not reachable); no AIPAC PAC committee contributions appear in his FEC committee-contribution records

others.name: American Task Force for Lebanon PAC — 2000–2008

statements.t: Declined to take a position on aid to Israel, saying the issue is complex and he is still listening to residents.

note.t: His Senate candidate financial disclosure (Senate eFD) was not reachable and not read. SEC insider data via GuruFocus show 32,265 Boston Scientific shares as of his last reported 2018 transaction (about $1.4M at the page's price); current holdings unknown. Boston Scientific paid new directors about $60,000 a year plus about $120,000 in stock when he joined in 2009. A Democratic legislator, citing his disclosure, said his income grew from $1 million in 2009 to as much as $35 million; that partisan description is unverified here.

committees: Senate (2003–09): Finance; Commerce, Science and Transportation; Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs; Joint Economic Committee

revolving.t: Joined the Washington law and lobbying firm in July 2010, about 18 months after leaving the Senate. Whether he registered as a lobbyist was not checked (Senate LDA database not reached).
Joined the medical-device maker's board in March 2009, two months after leaving the Senate. Boston Scientific's corporate PAC gave $5,000 to his 2026 campaign (June 23, 2026).
Former director of the cable company; SEC data show a 100-share purchase in Sept. 2010. As a senator he sat on the Commerce Committee, which oversees telecommunications.

democracy.t: Voted Nay on the objection to Ohio's 2004 electoral votes (voted to count them).

note.t: Born in Boston in 1964; his family is based in New Hampshire, where his father became governor in 1983. He lives in Rye. The years he has lived in the state are not documented in the sources opened.

checks.legal: Courts: CourtListener and Justia could not be reached from this research tool, and no web-search budget remained for a news search on lawsuits, so courts were not searched ('no'). No lawsuit, charge or ethics finding appears in Wikipedia or the race coverage opened (AP, NHPR, Concord Monitor, Fox News, NH Bulletin). Wikipedia notes the 2002 New Hampshire Democratic phone-jamming scandal during his first Senate race was organized by Republican party operatives; it does not say he was involved, so it isn't listed as his record. Ethics: Senate Ethics Committee records not searched ('no').
checks.foreign: FARA: bulk FARA files searched by exact name on 2026-10-13; no row names him. Senate financial disclosure (foreign assets/income) not read. Lloyd's of London council seat is documented on Wikipedia and Boston Scientific's bio.
checks.claims: His campaign site (sununusenator.com) could not be opened, so the mechanical sample (about page, issues page, top ads) could not be run. Instead: every checkable factual claim in his own words in the news coverage opened (Fox News interview 2026-09-17, NHPR/AP primary coverage, AP launch story, Citizens Count issue summary). 8 rated; ads not identified.
checks.democracy: Senate roll call 1 of the 109th Congress (Jan. 6, 2005) from the records file. He was not in office in Jan. 2017 or Jan. 2021. No public statement by him on the 2020 or 2024 results was found in the sources opened; no dedicated search was possible.

foreign.t: Appointed to the governing council of Lloyd's of London (U.K. insurance market) on Jan. 30, 2019; still listed as a council member.

recordx.note: Not a sitting member, so no current missed-vote rate. His Senate candidate disclosure (timeliness) and FEC RFAI/notices status could not be checked (efdsearch.senate.gov and fec.gov not reachable). recordx does not meet the two-item minimum; needs a human check.

corp.t: 2026: corporate PACs gave $67,000 (e.g. Goldman Sachs $10,000, Koch Inc. $7,500, NSSF $7,500, Boston Scientific $5,000, ExxonMobil $2,500) and trade PACs $31,000. Career: $2.55M from corporate PACs and $994,453 from trade PACs. Americans for Prosperity Action, a Koch-network super PAC, spent about $6.3M supporting him in 2026.

lobby.t: PACs organized around other countries' policy gave in his 2000–2008 campaigns: Arab American Leadership Council PAC $24,000, American Task Force for Lebanon PAC $13,050, NORPAC (pro-Israel) $10,000, U.S.-Cuba Democracy PAC $7,500 and ARMENPAC $1,000. None in 2026 FEC data.

research_notes: ACCESS: fec.gov, efdsearch.senate.gov, congress.gov, Track AIPAC, CourtListener and his campaign site were not fetchable (only pages that appeared in the 12 permitted searches, plus Wikipedia, could be opened). Money uses the on-disk FEC records file (data as of 2026-10-13; 2026 coverage through 2026-08-19). MONEY: pac_biz = corporate $67,000 + trade $31,000 + membership $25,000 + cooperative $5,000; pac_ideo = leadership PACs $288,500 + ideological $35,500; other = candidate committee $5,000. These come to $457,000 vs. the FEC total of $417,000 for PACs and committees; the difference wasn't resolved. The FEC party figure of $62,000 is direct NRSC money; NRSC coordinated expenditures of $5,257,129 are listed as outside support. Receipts of $4.18M exceed individuals + PACs + party ($2.88M); the rest (likely joint-fundraising transfers) is not broken out. NH Bulletin reported $4.1M raised and 57.5% from individuals. instate_pct 0.144 = 1 minus the 85.6% out-of-state share OpenSecrets reported for his latest report (via NH Bulletin), not the whole cycle. The 2026 committee-contribution file also shows $232,950 to his old Senate committee S0NH00201 in 2026, not reconciled. Outside spending is FEC Schedule E through about Oct. 1, 2026; super PAC donor lists not checked. 'Lobby' PACs and the 'Arab American' PAC are classed by name in the records file. ISRAEL: he has no Israel votes from the key-vote period (left office 2009); historical Senate Israel votes were not compiled. NOT FOUND: Senate financial disclosure / net worth; Akin Gump lobbying registration; debates (none reported in sources opened; access counts omitted); town halls; his ads. A NH Democratic Party post links him to a Doha event mentioned in an Epstein email; that is a partisan claim with no independent documentation in this pass, and it is not included as a finding. The Pappas campaign's 'real job' attack (Dec. 2025) cites only an X post, which was not opened.
